buildings.name: Cathedral of Aachen
buildings.audience: Players fighting with their attacking army in GBG
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold adds a 7% attack multiplier for your attacking army in GBG. It reaches 13% at 500; compare that extra benefit with the cost of further levels.

buildings.name: Statue of Zeus
buildings.audience: Guild Expedition attackers
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold adds a 4% attack-and-defense multiplier for GE attackers. Copper already provides +320% attack. The Gold multiplier reaches a displayed 7% at 401 and remains 7% at 500.

buildings.name: Seed Vault
buildings.audience: GBG defending-army players, with extra rewards for daily aiding
buildings.guidance: The 3% GBG defending-army multiplier at level 201 makes Seed Vault a strong choice for that army. It reaches 5% at 500. Improved Helping Hands adds a 15% chance at 201, rising to 25% at 500; its value depends on how often you aid and on the reward pool.

buildings.name: Observatory
buildings.audience: Guild treasury contributors
buildings.guidance: At level 201, the adjacent-era guild-goods output is 687 per day and the GE defending-army defense multiplier is 3%. At 500 these reach 1,160 and 5%. Review the goods benefit against your guild’s needs.

buildings.name: Château Frontenac
buildings.audience: Regular Heroic Tavern quest players
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold boosts Heroic Tavern rewards by 53%, compared with 100% at 500. This is separate from the Copper quest bonus; its value depends on how often you complete Heroic Tavern quests.

buildings.name: The Arc
buildings.audience: Frequent contributors to other players’ Great Buildings
buildings.guidance: At level 201, the Copper contribution bonus is 100% and the Gold contribution bonus is 23%. They apply to different destination tiers. Gold reaches 40% at 500; more contribution volume makes the later gains more useful.
notes: The older tracker’s Basic Contribution wording mentions the first 200 levels. That cutoff predates the October 8 redesign; the guide uses the new Copper/Gold destination-tier distinction.

buildings.name: Space Carrier
buildings.audience: GE attackers or players who still need special goods
buildings.guidance: At level 201, the GE attacking-army multiplier is 8% and the special-goods production boost is 18%. Their level 500 values are 15% and 30%; evaluate both against the activities you use.

buildings.name: Castel del Monte
buildings.audience: Players who value daily FP or actively fight in Quantum Incursions
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Copper provides 800 FP per day and Gold adds a 6% QI attacking-army attack multiplier. The QI multiplier is a lower-priority reason to invest, making Castel del Monte a situational choice. It reaches a displayed 10% at 401 and stays 10% at 500.

buildings.name: The Kraken
buildings.audience: Players who regularly fight two-wave battles
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Second Strike has an 18% chance over 164 eligible battles per day, versus 30% over 300 at 500. If you do fewer two-wave battles, extra attempts may go unused.

buildings.name: The Blue Galaxy
buildings.audience: Players with valuable city collections; Gold mainly for active QI players
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Copper provides a 75% double-collection chance over 15 city collections per day. Gold provides 33% over 6 QI collections, rising to 60% over 10 at 500. Further Gold levels mainly matter to active QI players.

buildings.name: St. Mark's Basilica
buildings.audience: Cities with substantial goods production
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold boosts eligible goods production by 15%, compared with 25% at 500. Its value depends on how much your eligible buildings already produce.

buildings.name: Alcatraz
buildings.audience: Active Guild Battlegrounds fighters
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold combines an 8% attacking-army multiplier with +430% attack and defense for both armies in GBG. At 500 those become 15% and +750%. Copper already produces 750 units per day.

buildings.name: Arctic Orangery
buildings.audience: Players who value daily FP and critical hits
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Copper provides 2,000 FP per day and a 50% same-age critical chance. Gold adds a 23% critical chance against units of a different age, rising to 40% at 500. Rogues do not benefit from that Gold effect.

buildings.name: Colosseum
buildings.audience: Players with valuable Military Historical Allies
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold adds 6 effective levels to placed Military Historical Allies. This reaches a displayed +10 at 401 and stays +10 at 500. The value depends on the allies you have placed.

buildings.name: Deal Castle
buildings.audience: Quantum Incursion defending-army players
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold adds a 6% attack multiplier for your defending army in QI. It reaches a displayed 10% at 401 and stays 10% at 500. This effect does not help your attacking army.

buildings.name: Himeji Castle

rows.match: Scope conflict — screenshot + tracker differ from announcement

buildings.audience: GBG defending-army players and frequent main-city fighters
buildings.guidance: The 3% GBG defending-army multiplier at level 201 makes Himeji Castle a strong candidate. Its exact scope still needs verification: the icon suggests attack and defense, while the official text says defense only. Enhanced Spoils of War adds an 18% chance over 53 eligible battles per day, rising to 30% over 100 at 500; its reward pool is not shown.
notes: Scope conflict: the screenshot’s GBG icon matches the tracker’s defending-army attack-and-defense multiplier. The October 8 announcement calls it defense only. Values are transcribed, but verify the in-game tooltip before counting an attack benefit.

buildings.name: Lotus Temple
buildings.audience: Players using Science Historical Allies or GE defending armies
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Gold adds 6 effective Science Ally levels and an 8% GE defending-army multiplier. At 500 these reach +10 levels and 15%. Consider the allies you have placed and which GE army you use.

buildings.name: Royal Albert Hall
buildings.audience: Cities keeping goods buildings from useful eras
buildings.guidance: At level 201, Goods Reserve shows 2,585 goods per day, compared with 5,000 at 500. The goods types depend on the goods buildings placed in your city, so check your eligible mix first.

buildings.name: Shattered Horizon Siphon
buildings.audience: Frequent Gold-tier contributors
buildings.guidance: At level 201, the Gold contribution bonus is 28%, rising to 50% at 500. Copper already provides a 5% multiplier for both armies. Later levels are most relevant to players making many Gold-tier contributions.
notes: The older tracker’s Basic Contribution wording mentions the first 200 levels. That cutoff predates the October 8 redesign; the guide uses the new Copper/Gold destination-tier distinction.

buildings.name: Terracotta Army
buildings.audience: Players using both armies in Guild Expedition
buildings.guidance: At level 201, each GE army receives a 7% Gold multiplier, versus 12% at 500. Copper already provides +700% attack and defense for both armies. Value each Gold effect according to the armies you actually use.

buildings.name: The Virgo Project
buildings.audience: Two-wave fighters or QI attacking-army players
buildings.guidance: At level 201, the second-wave effect has a 13% chance across 116 eligible battles per day, and the QI attacking-army defense multiplier is 3%. At 500 these reach 20% across 200 battles and 5%.

buildings.name: A.I. Core
buildings.audience: Players collecting eligible special-goods productions
buildings.guidance: Level 101 shows a 43% bonus over 9 eligible collections, versus 50% over 10 at 200. Before Arctic Future the client describes a supplies variant; check which version applies to you.
notes: The image shows a percentage and collection count, without /24h. No daily refresh rate has been inferred from the image.

buildings.name: Capitol
buildings.audience: Cities with an actual population or supplies shortage
buildings.guidance: Its roles are population and supplies. There is no Gold unlock to chase; compare its footprint with the city buildings you could use instead.

buildings.name: Cape Canaveral
buildings.audience: Players who want straightforward daily FP
buildings.guidance: The shown output grows from 163 FP per day at 101 to 200 at 200: an extra 37 per day. Upgrade costs are needed to decide whether those 99 levels pay back.

buildings.name: Atomium
buildings.audience: Guild-focused players who also need happiness
buildings.guidance: Guild goods rise from 324 per day at 101 to 397 at 200. There is no Gold effect, so further investment only improves the existing two outputs.

buildings.name: Atlantis Museum
buildings.audience: Players who regularly plunder
buildings.guidance: The double-plunder chance rises from 43% at 101 to 50% at 200. If plundering is not part of your play, the distinctive bonus adds little value.

buildings.name: Cosmic Catalyst
buildings.audience: Same-age fighters and guild contributors
buildings.guidance: At level 101, it provides a 22% same-age critical chance and 814 guild goods per day. Level 200 raises these to 25% and 1,000. Assess it alongside your other critical-hit sources; these screenshots do not establish their combined stacking rule.

buildings.name: Flying Island
buildings.audience: Active cultural-settlement players
buildings.guidance: The shard chance is already 46% at 101 versus 52% at 200. The images do not show reward rarity or value, so a higher chance alone is not enough to establish payback.

buildings.name: Galata Tower
buildings.audience: Players who need protection against plundering
buildings.guidance: At 101 it shows 57% repel chance for 5 attempts; at 200, 64% for 6. Build for that specific protection rather than for a future tier unlock.

buildings.name: Gaea Statue
buildings.audience: Cities short of happiness or medals
buildings.guidance: Only happiness and medals are shown, with no Gold expansion. Check whether these resources are actually limiting your city before allocating space and FP.

buildings.name: Frauenkirche of Dresden
buildings.audience: Cities that still need goods and happiness
buildings.guidance: Goods production moves from 340 per day at 101 to 414 at 200. There is no distinct new mechanic to unlock beyond those existing outputs.

buildings.name: Hagia Sophia
buildings.audience: Players who need both FP and happiness
buildings.guidance: The last shown stretch adds 22 FP per day, from 98 at 101 to 120 at 200. Compare the benefit with its footprint and your current happiness needs.

buildings.name: Innovation Tower
buildings.audience: Cities with a population shortage
buildings.guidance: Daily FP rises from 98 to 120 between 101 and 200, alongside more population. Extra population is useful only if your city needs it.

buildings.name: Lighthouse of Alexandria
buildings.audience: Players collecting many supply buildings
buildings.guidance: Its main advantage depends on using the 40 boosted supply collections. Without that routine, evaluate it mainly as a goods producer; it has no Gold tier.

buildings.name: Rain Forest Project
buildings.audience: Active aiders seeking Copper blueprints
buildings.guidance: The 787% at 101 and 958% at 200 are increases to the normal blueprint chance, not literal drop probabilities. No Gold blueprint production is shown.

buildings.name: Notre Dame
buildings.audience: Cities short of supplies and happiness
buildings.guidance: Only basic city resources are shown. Existing event-building alternatives and available space should determine whether this still has a role.

buildings.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
buildings.audience: Players specifically building their defending army
buildings.guidance: It reaches +106% defending-army attack and defense at 101 versus +125% at 200. It does not provide an attacking-army bonus or a Gold upgrade.

buildings.name: Saturn VI Gate CENTAURUS
buildings.audience: Attacking-army players who need previous-era goods
buildings.guidance: At level 101, it combines +651% attacking-army attack and defense with 894 previous-era goods per day. At 200 those reach +800% and 1,095 goods. Compare the extra benefit with the cost of the remaining levels.

buildings.name: Saturn VI Gate HYDRA
buildings.audience: Players using both armies and supporting their guild
buildings.guidance: At level 101, +488% attack and defense for both armies makes HYDRA a strong candidate, with 488 guild goods per day as an added benefit. At 200 these reach +600% and 600 goods. Review further levels against your combat needs and guild goals.

buildings.name: Saturn VI Gate PEGASUS
buildings.audience: Players who value FP and defending-army strength
buildings.guidance: At level 101, it provides 326 FP per day and +814% defending-army attack and defense. Level 200 adds 74 FP per day and raises the combat bonus to +1,000%. The combat effect does not help your attacking army.

buildings.name: Star Gazer
buildings.audience: Players with a specific previous-era goods shortage
buildings.guidance: The only shown effect produces 124 previous-era goods per day at 101 and 151 at 200. Check whether that output justifies the space in your city.

buildings.name: Space Needle
buildings.audience: Cities short of coins or happiness
buildings.guidance: The screenshot shows only coins and happiness. There is no new Gold ability that changes its role.

buildings.name: Stellar Warship
buildings.audience: Players wanting both-army strength and daily units
buildings.guidance: At level 101, it provides +814% attack and defense for both armies and 163 units per day. At 200 these reach +1,000% and 200 units. Review whether you need the extra combat strength and daily units.

buildings.name: Temple of Relics
buildings.audience: Players who complete many GE encounters
buildings.guidance: Relic chance rises from 31% at 101 to 35% at 200. More completed encounters make that extra chance more relevant; reward rarity is not shown here.

buildings.name: The Habitat
buildings.audience: Cities short of population or coins
buildings.guidance: The role remains population and coins, with no Gold tier. Invest only if those outputs solve a real constraint in your city.

buildings.name: Voyager V1
buildings.audience: Regular plunderers
buildings.guidance: The plunder-goods reward increases from 63 to 76 goods, with the same 3 attempts. Players who do not plunder will mainly receive supplies.

buildings.name: Truce Tower
buildings.audience: Frequent aiders seeking goods from aided buildings’ eras
buildings.guidance: The number of eligible aids rises from 192 at 101 to 229 at 200. Extra charges help only if you perform that many eligible aids.

buildings.name: Tower of Babel
buildings.audience: Early cities needing population and goods
buildings.guidance: Goods rise from 336 per day at 101 to 410 at 200. The absence of Gold keeps the decision focused on space, goods demand and population needs.

buildings.name: Oracle of Delphi
buildings.audience: Cities still needing starter supplies and happiness
buildings.guidance: This remains a basic supplies-and-happiness building. There is no later special effect to justify leveling it purely for a future unlock.

methodology.values: Manually read and verified against all 49 original screenshots. K/M rounding and charge counts are preserved.
methodology.icons: Screenshot artwork is matched to the frozen GB tracker client icon/text pairings. Historical GB/tier assignments are not reused.
methodology.recommendations: Gold buildings are reviewed at 201; Copper-only buildings at 101. Guidance considers benefits for the stated play style, not cost, efficiency or payback.
methodology.costs: No October 6 beta costs or live costs are mixed into this October 8 benefit guide.
methodology.footprints: Footprints come from the existing GBAnalysis building metadata, not these screenshots.
methodology.gaps: Only the shown levels are transcribed. Gold screenshots show 201, while the official Copper growth cap is 200. No intermediate values are interpolated.
